fields.description:
## Context

DSO maintainers shipping UI changes operate without any agent that actually sees rendered pixels — all visual judgment is mediated through SVG/JSON and LLM text reasoning. Spatial-quality issues (whitespace, element density, alignment grid adherence, visual hierarchy legibility, intent-match drift between design spec and rendered output) ship unenforced. The existing design-systems-lead committee reviewer's `visual_hierarchy` dimension is LLM-text-based and misses pixel-observable failures. This epic introduces a multimodal visual-evaluator agent, an orchestrator skill that captures Playwright screenshots at routes from `.ui-discovery-cache/route-map.json`, two sprint integration points (inline per-task iteration loop + post-batch reviewer), a 5th ui-designer committee reviewer that owns the pixel-observable legibility dimension, and a labeled calibration corpus that grounds the agent's attribution-class accuracy before downstream automation depends on it.

The original UI/UX quality proposal labeled this "highest-leverage single addition" among five complementary plans (A-E). This epic ships Plan B as its own focused unit; Plans A (115c DESIGN.md linter), C (77a3 spatial metrics co-processor), D (d29f Storybook component isolation), and E (7ce2 semantic spatial-intent grafting) ship as separate complementary epics linked via relates_to. Epic 4f8e (Figma perceptual diff) answers a different question (pixel-regression vs. quality) and ships independently. Epic 53ee (completion-verifier conformance) operates at a different gate timing (closure vs. task) and ships independently.

EPIC_CLASS: class:architectural

## Success Criteria

1. The visual-evaluator agent at `plugins/dso/agents/visual-evaluator.md` runs at temperature=0 and emits JSON conforming to the schema `{scores: {whitespace_balance, element_density, visual_hierarchy_legibility, alignment_grid_adherence, intent_match} (each 1-5), findings: [{bounding_box, dom_xpath, dom_cross_check_passed: bool, dimension, severity}], attribution_class: implementation_drift|design_flaw|mixed|uncertain, attribution_confidence: high|medium|low}` for PNG + design-manifest input. Every `bounding_box` is cross-checked against the rendered DOM via Playwright `getBoundingClientRect`; findings with `dom_cross_check_passed: false` are auto-downgraded to `severity: low` and excluded from blocking attribution routing. The agent prompt includes a written rubric plus at least three few-shot examples per `attribution_class`. A schema-validation + DOM-cross-check regression test asserts the output shape and cross-check behavior on at least one fixture PNG.

2. The visual-evaluator skill at `plugins/dso/skills/visual-evaluator/SKILL.md` emits an `EMIT-PRECONDITIONS` landmark before activating each integration point. Integration A (inline) and Integration B (post-batch) activate only when preconditions are satisfied: `project_type=web`, `playwright_available`, `check-local-env.sh` exit 0, `route_map_fresh<24h` against `.ui-discovery-cache/route-map.json`. When preconditions fail, the degradation channel records the failure mode and the integration gate is reported as `not-applicable` (NOT silent soft-pass — explicit `visual_eval_inapplicable:<reason>` annotation on the ticket and on the integration gate's status). The skill captures Playwright screenshots at each route in `.ui-discovery-cache/route-map.json` with per-route metadata `{auth_required, viewports, themes, expected_status}`; a pre-capture health probe excludes non-200 routes from scoring (recorded as `visual_eval_excluded:non-200`). Captures default to light+dark and mobile+desktop variants unless route metadata declares a single mode. The design manifest is synthesized from `.claude/design-notes.md` + route metadata + task ticket body + Figma frame (when `design.figma_collaboration` enabled, graceful-degrade otherwise). Regression test: a fixture invocation against a known route produces the expected aggregated output; a fixture invocation with route map absent produces the `visual_eval_inapplicable` annotation rather than soft-pass; a 500-route fixture is excluded from scoring.

3. The calibration corpus at `plugins/dso/data/visual-eval-corpus/` contains at least 40 human-labeled balanced examples spanning the 4 attribution classes (at least 10 per class). Each fixture file is structured as `{screenshot.png, design_manifest.json, expected: {attribution_class, attribution_confidence, scores}, labeler_id, labeled_at}`. Commit-message-derived heuristic labels are excluded from the gate (allowed only as exploratory data, marked `provenance: heuristic`). The calibration script `plugins/dso/scripts/visual-eval-calibration.sh` runs the evaluator 3 times per fixture at temperature=0, computes median scores, asserts per-fixture score-variance ≤ 0.5, computes weighted attribution-class accuracy across the 4 classes, computes class-distribution skew (gate fails if any class is <10% or >60% of agent decisions on the corpus), and computes box-hallucination rate (percentage of findings with `dom_cross_check_passed: false`). The gate passes when ALL of: weighted attribution accuracy ≥ 0.7, every class within [10%, 60%] of agent decisions, every fixture score-variance ≤ 0.5, box-hallucination rate < 20%. Inter-rater agreement is recorded as Cohen's kappa across at least 2 labelers per fixture. Running the calibration script in the closing session exits 0 when all gate conditions hold.

4. Sprint Integration A (inline per-task iteration loop): `task-execution.md` invokes the visual-evaluator after sub-agent implementation. Per-finding attribution routing dispatches — `implementation_drift` at confidence high/medium → re-prompt the implementing sub-agent; `design_flaw` at confidence high/medium → re-dispatch `/dso:ui-designer`; `mixed | uncertain | low-confidence` → user dialog with bounding-box evidence (or `INTERACTIVITY_DEFERRED` annotation in non-interactive mode), capped at 2 user-dialog escalations per task with auto-defer beyond. Iteration cap = 2 (configurable via `visual_evaluator.iteration_cap`). Iteration-exhaustion failure mode is conditional: `intent_match` below `visual_evaluator.iteration_threshold` (default 3 of 5; configurable) blocks task closure; quality-dim-only shortfalls (`intent_match` ≥ threshold but any of the four pixel-observable dimensions < threshold) annotate the ticket `visual_debt:<dimension>` and proceed. **Dogfood verification**: replaying the calibration corpus's seed-PR set with Integration A enabled surfaces at least one spatial finding per PR that the text-mediated reviewer missed on at least 3 of the seed PRs (recorded in-session as part of the calibration script's output). Regression tests: a fixture task with sustained `intent_match` drift fails closure after 2 iterations; a fixture with quality-dim-only shortfall closes with a `visual_debt:` annotation; a fixture with 3 mixed/uncertain findings triggers auto-defer after the 2nd user-dialog escalation.

5. Sprint Integration B (post-batch) plus 5th ui-designer committee reviewer: a sprint step after `make test-visual` (or project `VISUAL_CMD`) dispatches the visual-evaluator at Opus 4.7 for the post-batch review pass. The new committee reviewer at `plugins/dso/skills/ui-designer/docs/reviewers/visual-spatial-evaluator.md` emits its own JSON at the same path/key shape as the existing 4 reviewers at `plugins/dso/skills/ui-designer/docs/reviewers/`. Design-systems-lead's `visual_hierarchy` dimension is fully removed; the new reviewer owns `visual_hierarchy_legibility` (pixel-observable), and design-systems-lead retains a separate `visual_hierarchy_intent` dimension (text reasoning about intent). Arbitration weighting and tie-break authority between `visual_hierarchy_intent` and `visual_hierarchy_legibility` are documented at `plugins/dso/skills/ui-designer/docs/arbitration.md` (or a chosen equivalent path): on conflicts about pixel-observable concerns, `visual_hierarchy_legibility` wins; on conflicts about intent-only concerns, `visual_hierarchy_intent` wins. Regression test: a Full-track UI design fixture produces a combined verdict from all 5 reviewers, arbitration produces a deterministic merged verdict, and visual-spatial-evaluator's verdict is structurally distinct from design-systems-lead's.

## State Lifecycle

| Variable | CREATE | UPDATE | CONSUME | RETIRE |
|----------|--------|--------|---------|--------|
| `plugins/dso/agents/visual-evaluator.md` | foundation story (wave 1) | future epics that refine agent contract | sprint task-execution.md (Integration A); sprint post-batch step (Integration B); ui-designer committee reviewer | never retired |
| `plugins/dso/skills/visual-evaluator/SKILL.md` | foundation story (wave 1) | future epics that refine orchestration logic | sprint task-execution.md (A); sprint post-batch step (B); standalone /dso:visual-evaluator invocation | never retired |
| `plugins/dso/skills/ui-designer/docs/reviewers/visual-spatial-evaluator.md` | committee-reviewer story (wave 3) | future epics that refine reviewer rubric | ui-designer committee arbitration | never retired |
| `plugins/dso/data/visual-eval-corpus/` directory | foundation story (wave 1) — seeded by at least 40 human-labeled examples | user-dialog disagreements append new labeled fixtures over time; relabeling events update individual fixtures | calibration script (SC3); regression tests | never retired — corpus grows over time |
| `.ui-discovery-cache/visual-eval/<key>.json` cache files | visual-evaluator skill on first dispatch per (screenshot-hash + agent-prompt-hash + design-manifest-hash) | overwritten on key changes | visual-evaluator skill on cache lookup | LRU-bounded by `visual_evaluator.cache_max_entries` (default 1000); evicted oldest-first |
| `dso-config.conf` keys: `visual_evaluator.iteration_threshold`, `visual_evaluator.success_median`, `visual_evaluator.cache_max_entries`, `visual_evaluator.iteration_cap` | foundation story (wave 1) writes defaults documentation in CONFIGURATION-REFERENCE.md | per-project tuning | visual-evaluator skill; sprint integration A/B; ui-designer reviewer | per-project lifecycle; never retired at plugin level |

## Scope (out)

- Visual-regression diffing against prior screenshots (separate epic; same Playwright + route-map infrastructure; out of scope here).
- Non-rendered Figma-only review (analyzing Figma frames without comparison to a rendered output).
- WCAG-contrast / ARIA / semantic accessibility (already owned by `accessibility-specialist.md` committee reviewer).
- Visual judgment for non-UI projects (CLI tools, libraries, backend services) — the preconditions contract reports `not-applicable` for these projects, so no false-compliance signal is emitted.
- Plans A, C, D, E from the same UI/UX proposal — separate complementary epics linked via `relates_to`.

## Dependencies

None. (Plan A's design-tokens-from-DESIGN.md may feed into Plan B's manifest synthesis when both ship; this is a sequencing optimization, not a hard dependency.)
